summary: Microsoft's Copilot chatbot falsely described a German court reporter as a convicted child abuser, a psychiatric escapee and a fraudster, apparently confusing the crimes he covered with his own history. It also gave his address and phone number. Removal attempts worked only briefly.
technical_summary: A search-integrated LLM assistant combined web content about court cases with the name of the journalist who reported on them, and generated defamatory claims plus personal contact details. Corrections by the vendor were temporary and the false output reappeared.

summary: A San Francisco cyclist alleges two driverless Waymo vehicles contributed to a crash in a bike lane: a passenger opened a door into her path and she was thrown into a second vehicle. She says she suffered serious injuries and that Waymo's passenger exit warning failed.
technical_summary: A robotaxi stopped beside a marked bike lane at a no-stopping curb and a passenger opened a door into the lane, while a second robotaxi entered the lane. The alleged failure was the Safe Exit warning system and drop-off controls, with no human driver to intervene.

technical_summary: Synthetic videos and images of real politicians were posted on Facebook pages ahead of an election. A fact-checking outlet ran them through an AI-detection platform that flagged them as AI-generated, and found the claims in them to be false.

summary: Microsoft reported that AI is helping fraudsters build fake shopping sites, reviews, deepfakes and phishing lures quickly and at scale. It said it blocked about 1.6 million bot signup attempts per hour and thwarted billions of dollars of fraud attempts over a year.
technical_summary: Threat actors use generative AI to scrape company data, generate fake storefronts, reviews, cloned voices and deepfakes, and automate account creation. This lowers the cost of fraud. Microsoft countered with detection models and browser protections.

notes: Aggregate threat report; reported fraud-attempt totals differ between sources ($4 billion vs $6.28 billion).

summary: A fake audio clip imitating President Biden's voice, apparently AI-generated, was shared on TikTok and X claiming he threatened to send F-15 fighter jets against Texas. The White House called the claim false and a forensics expert said the audio was likely AI-made.

summary: A class-action lawsuit alleges Cigna used an algorithm called PXDX to automatically reject over 300,000 patient claims in two months without individual review, as California law requires. Cigna says the tool only speeds up payments for common procedures.
technical_summary: An insurer's claims system compared procedure codes with diagnoses and flagged mismatches in batches, taking about 1.2 seconds per claim. Doctors allegedly signed off on denials in bulk without opening patient files. The company disputes the characterization.

summary: Twenty-six Meta employees sued, alleging internal AI-assisted systems used to rank workers for a May 2026 layoff disproportionately selected people on medical, pregnancy or family leave or with disabilities. Meta says layoff decisions were made by people, not AI.

Meta denies AI made the decisions; a court denied a temporary restraining order for lack of evidence.

summary: A criminal network in Bolivia used an AI-cloned voice of the education minister to convince job seekers that fake job offers were real, collecting payments by QR code. Authorities identified at least 19 victims and reported losses of more than 5 million bolivianos.
technical_summary: Scammers advertised fake government jobs on social media, then used a cloned voice of a public official on phone calls as proof of legitimacy before requesting an upfront payment. Voice synthesis served as a credibility tool in an employment fraud, partly run from prison.
